content.title: About
content.content: Steak is a cut of beef, typically taken from the rib, sirloin, or tenderloin. It has a rich, meaty flavor, firm texture, and a distinctive aroma that intensifies when seared over high heat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “steak” derives from the Old English “steik,” meaning a stick or spear, as early cuts were often impaled on rods.
The most popular doneness level is medium‑rare, where the internal temperature reaches about 55 °C.
In Japan, “sashimi‑steak” is served raw, sliced paper‑thin, and seasoned with soy and citrus.
Steak quality is often judged by marbling – the intramuscular fat that creates a buttery mouthfeel.
The world’s most expensive steak is Japanese Wagyu, which can reach a BMS (Beef Marbling Standard) of 12.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Steak provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Steak supplies B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals aid immune function and protect against oxidative stress.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Natural creatine in beef helps improve muscular energy production.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked steak can harbor pathogens such as E. coli or salmonella.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steak is typically grilled, pan‑seared, or oven‑roasted to the desired doneness. Let it rest for 5‑10 minutes after cooking so juices redistribute. Serve with sauces, vegetables, potatoes, or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh steak in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for 6‑12 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking.
